content:
Maria Chen: Quick FYI — noticed our weekly eng sync (recurring) showed as 9:00 AM PST for some folks and 5:00 PM CEST for others this morning. Also, after I edited the series to update agenda, the Zoom link reverted to the old meeting id for a few occurrences. Anyone else seeing this?

Sam Park: yup saw it. I joined the wrong meeting for a sec. :facepalm:

Alex Rivera: Calendar bug + DST + recurring Zoom meetings are the worst. What was the recurrence rule? Can you paste the exported RRULE?

Maria Chen: exported the event -> looked like: 
```
RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU;COUNT=52
```
Nothing crazy, but when I updated the series a few exceptions got created and Zoom re-provisioned different meeting ids for those instances.

calendar-bot: Heads-up: Zoom add-on may create a new meeting for edited instances. See https://support.zoom.us/hc/en-us/articles/360000000000/Recurring-meetings for guidance.

Lee Huang: Quick fix options: 1) Create a single recurring Zoom meeting (one meeting id) and put that id in the calendar description manually, 2) Recreate the GCal series and set the timezone to UTC in event settings so DST math is consistent.

Nora Patel: Also when you edit the series in GCal, choose "All events" and click "Update guests" — otherwise Google creates "this and following" which can lead to split instances.

Olivia Gomez: For a fast workaround I created a new series, disabled auto-provisioning in Zoom (so it doesn't replace the ID), and pasted the stable link in the event body. Posted link to #eng-notices so folks get the update.

Dave Brooks: Proposal: move the weekly eng sync to 16:00 UTC. That covers NA mornings and EU afternoons. Maria, can you recreate the series and paste the stable Zoom link? I can sweep calendar conflicts after.

Maria Chen: Will do. Plan: recreate series at 16:00 UTC, disable Zoom auto-provisioning (use fixed meeting id), put meeting id + dial-in in the description, and make sure timezone in event details is set to UTC. I'll post confirmation here when complete. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
